source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
When transplanting seedlings out of nursery trays, farmers should carefully press or push from underneath each cell to release the seedling and its root ball intact, taking care not to break or damage the roots. Handling should be gentle so the root ball and surrounding growing medium stay together around the roots.

Seedlings should be planted into the previously prepared field planting holes (in the plastic-mulched or straw-mulched bed) at a depth level with the top of the seedling's root ball — planted neither too deep nor too shallow — and then lightly firmed with soil around the base and watered in immediately after transplanting to help the seedling establish and recover from transplant shock quickly. Transplanting is best done in the cooler part of the day (early morning or late afternoon) to reduce stress on the young plants.
